regime: Sticky, energy-led inflation with a stalling labor market and a Fed still hiking; long yields above 5% and stretched valuations
summary: The most likely regime 6-12 months out is late-cycle stagflation-lite: headline inflation held up by oil near $100, core PCE around 3%, payroll growth near zero, and a Fed that hikes once or twice more (futures imply about 4.6% by mid-2027) before pausing. With the 10Y at 5.1% and equity risk premiums negative, long-duration and AI-capex-financed growth is the most fragile part of the market, while companies with pricing power, cash returns or direct exposure to energy and defense budgets should hold up better. The model portfolio leans to quality health care, energy services and midstream, P&C insurance, defense, a staples compounder and selective grid/power equipment, entered on pullbacks to support rather than chased.
drivers: Oil supply risk around Hormuz and Russia sanctions keeps WTI near $90-105
Fed futures price a December hike (92%) and about 4.6% by June 2027
10Y Treasury at 5.1% (98th 10-year percentile) with a negative equity risk premium
Payrolls 3-month average +51k: weak hiring but low firing (claims 199k)
AI capex continues but financing stress (CoreWeave credit) pressures semis and neoclouds
Energy and health care lead SPY by 14pp and 7.5pp over 3 months
risks: Iran/Hormuz de-escalation drops oil below $80 and reverses energy leadership
Fed overtightens into a labor contraction (claims above 250k), hurting cyclicals and insurers' equity books
A sharp AI-led equity de-rating drags everything, including defensives, given 258% market cap/GDP
A rally in long bonds (10Y below 4.6%) would favour the growth names this portfolio underweights

themes.name: Energy supply squeeze
themes.why: Oil near $100 with a structural supply risk premium; services and midstream benefit from higher activity and volumes without needing new highs in crude.

themes.name: Quality health care
themes.why: Defensive earnings growth independent of the rate cycle; the sector leads SPY by 7.5pp over 3 months and 11.6pp over 6 months.

themes.name: Higher-for-longer financials
themes.why: P&C insurers earn more on float when short rates stay above 4% and have pricing power in an inflationary claims environment.

themes.name: Defense and geopolitics
themes.why: Middle East conflict and Houthi attacks support defense budgets and munitions demand.

themes.name: Defensive consumer compounder
themes.why: A weak-sentiment, high-price consumer trades down to membership warehouse retail; staples lead SPY by 5.6pp over 1 month.

themes.name: Power and grid build-out
themes.why: Electricity demand from data centres and grid replacement persists even if AI financing slows; a 24% pullback resets the entry.

candidates.thesis: Oilfield services lag crude (SLB -18.6% from its high while WTI is +72% y/y), so a higher-for-longer oil price should lift international and offshore activity and earnings estimates. Basing in Stage 1 above a 4-touch support at 47.5.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 44.5 (breaks the 47.5 support base) or WTI back below $80 on a durable Hormuz settlement.

candidates.thesis: Gas pipelines with fee-based cash flows benefit from LNG exports and power-generation demand from data centres; trading at a 6-touch support (68.4) in a flat base with an analyst target of 85.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 65.5 (loses the 68.4 support base).

candidates.thesis: Obesity-drug volume growth gives earnings growth that does not depend on the economic cycle; Minervini 7/7 Stage 2 leader in the strongest sector. Buy a pullback toward the 50-day average rather than at the highs.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 1085 (under the 1094.5 support) or a material GLP-1 pricing/policy shock.

candidates.thesis: Low-beta pharma and medtech cash flows with a dividend; pulled back 9.5% from its high to stacked supports at 249.8 and 243.2 while still in Stage 2.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 236 (breaks the 243.2 support).

candidates.thesis: Short rates above 4% boost investment income on float, and personal auto pricing keeps pace with claims inflation; forward P/E 13.4 at a 6-touch support near 216.5 and the 50-day average.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 206 (loses the 207.4 support) or a sharp rise in loss ratios in monthly results.

candidates.thesis: Middle East conflict and depleted munitions stockpiles support multi-year defense demand; forward P/E 16.9, 19% below its high, holding a 5-touch support at 548.9 above the 50-day average.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 524 (loses the 548.9 support and the 50-day average).
catalysts: Government funding and defense budget headlines

candidates.thesis: Membership retail gains share when consumer sentiment is at the 5th percentile and prices are high; trading on an 11-touch support near 996 and back above its 200-day average.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 925 (breaks the 926.9 support) or slowing membership renewal rates.
catalysts: Monthly sales reports (early November, date n/a)
Q1 FY27 results in December (date n/a)

candidates.thesis: Gas turbines, grid equipment and electrification have multi-year backlogs tied to power demand rather than AI financing alone; the stock is 24% off its high at a 6-touch support near 877 with an analyst target of 1224.
candidates.invalidation: A daily close below 835 (loses the 877 support) or order cancellations tied to data-centre financing stress.
